chapter_title: Concerning the Interpretation of the Fourteen [Great Aeons] of Light, about which Sethel has spoken in [his Prayer]
chapter_note: Short hermeneutical chapter structured as interpretation of Seth's prayer. The oldest teaching layer is a fourteen-fold enumeration of cosmic entities and their cosmological function — a systematic degree-mapping. The editorial overlay is the identification of these entities with 'praises' in Seth's prayer and the dialogue framing. The chapter's substrate content is concentrated in ¶3-5, with the enumeration (5 elements + call/hearing + 5 sons of Living Spirit + 2 fathers = 14) forming the structural backbone. The final paragraph, though heavily lacunose, contains significant cosmological description of the Ambassador's role. The negative editorial fatigue score reflects the frame-heavy opening giving way to denser teaching in the second half.

paragraphs.core_text: what are the [f]ourteen grea[t a]eons of light?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame formula ('Once again the disciples question the apostle. They sa[y] to him: We be[seech] you, our master, that you may enlighten us a[bou]t this lesson that is wr[itten in]'), the citation from Seth's prayer ('the prayer of Sethel, the first-born son of [Ad]am. As he says: You are glorious, you fourteen great [ae]ons of [lig]ht'), and honorific address ('Tell us, our master'). Retained the substantive cosmological question that defines the teaching topic.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Heavy dialogue frame vocabulary (24.59). The citation of Seth's prayer is an editorial hermeneutic act — it places the teaching within a textual tradition. The substantive question about the fourteen aeons reveals the teaching structure.

Pure dialogue attribution with first-person authority claim ('I am the one who will interpret for you'). No cosmological teaching content — only the speaker asserting interpretive authority. The reference to 'the fourteen great aeons of light about which he has spoken' merely echoes the question without adding teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: the [ ... ] below abide in fourteen [great aeons ...]: the five elements, the sons of the First Man, together with the call and the hearing. They anoint them, living in them. These shall make seven, five plus two.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed pedagogical frame marker 'Happen you know this, that' — addressed to audience ('you'), functioning as dialogue frame. Retained all enumeration and cosmological process description.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic enumeration — five elements + call + hearing = seven. This is the first half of a fourteen-fold degree structure. 'They anoint them, living in them' describes a cosmic process (indwelling/anointing relationship between these entities). The enumeration arithmetic ('These shall make seven, five plus two') is characteristic of substrate list-teaching. Substrate score 13.04 confirms.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... the] f[ive s]ons of the Living Spirit who [support] all [the wei]ght of the universe; together with the [Li]vi[ng] Spirit [and the Fir]st Man, their fathers. [...] by which the universe is established.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed editorial hermeneutic connection to Seth's prayer: 'These are the fourt[een p]raises that he has proclaimed, the praise that is made of fourteen pra[yers]' — this identifies the cosmic entities with 'praises' in the cited text, an interpretive act. Retained the cosmological function statement 'by which the universe is established' as it describes what these entities DO within the cosmic system.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the fourteen-fold enumeration: 5 sons of Living Spirit + Living Spirit + First Man (the two fathers) = 7, totaling 14 with ¶3. The supporting function ('support all the weight of the universe') and establishing function are cosmological process descriptions — both sides stay within the system. The Seth prayer identification is the editorial overlay binding substrate teaching to the hermeneutical frame.

paragraphs.core_text: [There are fourt]een aeons of light [ ... ] [...the la]nd that is not revealed. This land [ ... ... is estab]lished. They bore up under the enemy [ ... ... equa]ls them. The hidden plenitude that [ ... ] the Ambassador who came from the Father, the [ ... ] He came and stood firm in the midst of these [ ... ]: he is called the good father of [all] the ae[ons and gods] who are holy and conjoined. He has become leader and a great king after the likeness of the first Father, the lord of all these cou[nse]ls. This universe is held together by their will [ ... ] to the end of all things.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed editorial reference to Seth's prayer: 'of Seth [e] ... ] about them in his prayer, for they are expl[ai]ned [ ... ]' — this connects the cosmological content back to the hermeneutical frame of interpreting Seth's text.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Dense cosmological content despite heavy lacunae. Describes: (1) cosmic geography — 'the land that is not revealed'; (2) cosmic conflict — 'bore up under the enemy'; (3) emanation — 'the Ambassador who came from the Father'; (4) cosmic kingship — 'leader and a great king after the likeness of the first Father'; (5) cosmic function — 'This universe is held together by their will.' All mappings stay within the cosmic system. The Ambassador's role as king 'after the likeness of the first Father' is a degree-mapping (image of the eternal Father). The 'hidden plenitude' is cosmic geography terminology. Institutional score (1.48) is noise from 'father/lord' terminology that is cosmological here.
